author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of meditation upon the hidden judgments of God, that we may not be lifted up because of our well-doing

notes.text: (1) Job xv. 15. (2) Isaiah xxix. 16. (3) Psalm cxvii. 2.

verses.text: Thou sendest forth Thy judgments against me, O Lord, and shakest all my bones with fear and trembling, and my soul trembleth exceedingly.
verses.modernizedText: You send forth Your judgments against me, O Lord, and shake all my bones with fear and trembling, and my soul trembles exceedingly.

verses.text: I stand astonished, and remember that the heavens are not clean in thy sight.(1) If Thou chargest Thine angels with folly, and didst spare them not, how shall it be unto me?
verses.modernizedText: I stand astonished, and remember that the heavens are not clean in Your sight.(1) If You charge Your angels with folly, and did not spare them, how will it be with me?

verses.text: Stars have fallen from heaven, and what shall I dare who am but dust?
verses.modernizedText: Stars have fallen from heaven, and what shall I dare who am but dust?

verses.text: They whose works seemed to be praiseworthy, fell into the lowest depths, and they who did eat Angels’ food, them have I seen delighted with the husks that the swine do eat.
verses.modernizedText: Those whose works seemed to be praiseworthy fell into the lowest depths, and those who ate Angels’ food, I have seen delighting in the husks that the swine eat.

verses.text: There is therefore no holiness, if Thou O Lord, withdraw Thine hand.
verses.modernizedText: There is therefore no holiness, if You, O Lord, withdraw Your hand.

verses.text: No wisdom profiteth, if Thou leave off to guide the helm.
verses.modernizedText: No wisdom profits, if You stop guiding the helm.

verses.text: No strength availeth, if Thou cease to preserve.
verses.modernizedText: No strength avails, if You cease to preserve.

verses.text: No purity is secure, if Thou protect it not.
verses.modernizedText: No purity is secure, if You do not protect it.

verses.text: No self-keeping availeth, if Thy holy watching be not there.
verses.modernizedText: No guarding of oneself avails, if Your holy watching is not there.

verses.text: For when we are left alone we are swallowed up and perish, but when we are visited, we are raised up, and we live.
verses.modernizedText: For when we are left alone we are swallowed up and perish, but when we are visited, we are raised up, and we live.

verses.text: For indeed we are unstable, but are made strong through Thee; we grow cold, but are rekindled by Thee.
verses.modernizedText: For indeed we are unstable, but are made strong through You; we grow cold, but are rekindled by You.

verses.text: Oh, how humbly and abjectly must I reckon of myself, how must I weigh it as nothing, if I seem to have nothing good!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how humbly and abjectly must I reckon myself, how must I weigh it as nothing, if I seem to have nothing good!

verses.text: Oh, how profoundly ought I to submit myself to Thy unfathomable judgments, O Lord, when I find myself nothing else save nothing, and again nothing!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how profoundly ought I to submit myself to Your unfathomable judgments, O Lord, when I find myself nothing else but nothing, and again nothing!

verses.text: Oh weight unmeasurable, oh ocean which cannot be crossed over, where I find nothing of myself save nothing altogether!
verses.modernizedText: Oh immeasurable weight, oh ocean which cannot be crossed over, where I find nothing of myself but nothing altogether!

verses.text: Where, then, is the hiding-place of glory, where the confidence begotten of virtue?
verses.modernizedText: Where, then, is the hiding place of glory, where the confidence born of virtue?

verses.text: All vain-glory is swallowed up in the depths of Thy judgments against me.
verses.modernizedText: All vainglory is swallowed up in the depths of Your judgments against me.

verses.text: What is all flesh in Thy sight?
verses.modernizedText: What is all flesh in Your sight?

verses.text: For how shall the clay boast against Him that fashioned it?(2) How can he be lifted up in vain speech whose heart is subjected in truth to God?
verses.modernizedText: For how shall the clay boast against Him who fashioned it?(2) How can he be lifted up in vain speech whose heart is subjected in truth to God?

verses.text: The whole world shall not lift him up whom Truth hath subdued; nor shall he be moved by the mouth of all who praise him, who hath placed all his hope in God.
verses.modernizedText: The whole world will not lift up him whom Truth has subdued; nor will he who has placed all his hope in God be moved by the mouth of all who praise him.

verses.text: For they themselves who speak, behold, they are all nothing; for they shall cease with the sound of their words, but the truth of the Lord endureth for ever.(3)
verses.modernizedText: For those who speak, behold, they themselves are all nothing; for they will cease with the sound of their words, but the truth of the Lord endures forever.(3)
